facts.fact: Pátzcuaro has pre-Hispanic Purépecha roots and a colonial urban history. Its traditional construction uses adobe, stone, wood and clay roof tiles; this is historical/architectural context, not a claim about every current building.
facts.excerpt: adobe, la piedra, la madera y tejas
facts.location: Historical overview, paragraph about traditional architecture

facts.fact: INAH identifies Plaza Vasco de Quiroga as Plaza Grande and Plaza Gertrudis Bocanegra as Plaza Chica. It lists the former Dominican convent, now Casa de los Once Patios, the Sagrario and the Basilica among the historic religious buildings. INAH also records Gertrudis Bocanegra’s participation in the Independence movement, supporting the square’s civic-memory context.
facts.excerpt: la Plaza Vasco de Quiroga o Plaza grande, la Plaza Gertrudis Bocanegra o Plaza chica
facts.location: Overview of open spaces and religious buildings

facts.fact: The national Zona de Monumentos Históricos was declared on 19 December 1990. This designation is not used to claim a present UNESCO World Heritage inscription.

The devotion to Nuestra Señora de la Salud is associated with a cane-paste image commissioned by Vasco de Quiroga in 1539, according to INAH. This describes religious heritage, not medical efficacy or current visitor access.

INAH links eighteenth-century commercial and copper-mining wealth to substantial houses around the main square, with pink quarry-stone ornament on columns, portal arches and façades. This is a historical explanation, not a construction-date claim for every present building.
facts.location: Historical overview, paragraph about eighteenth-century economic growth and mansions around the main square
